items.name: FOOD_NEED_ADULT
items.text: Food an adult eats per year. A child (under ADULT_AGE) eats FOOD_NEED_CHILD.

items.name: FOOD_NEED_CHILD
items.text: Food a child eats per year.

items.name: ADULT_AGE
items.text: Age at which a person works and eats like an adult.

items.name: SKILL_MAX
items.text: Skills run from 1 to this; production formulas use skill / SKILL_MAX.

items.name: REGEN_BASE
items.text: Each year an island's wild food and wood regrow this share (x the island's regeneration rate) of the gap to their highest value.

items.name: SCARCITY_LOSS
items.text: World scarcity 1.0 cuts farm output and the stock maxima by this share.

items.name: TOOL_BONUS
items.text: Output rises by this share while a person holds a tool; tools wear out by TOOL_WEAR a year.

items.name: SHORTAGE_DAMAGE
items.text: Health lost at a 100% food shortfall; a fully fed year heals RECOVERY.

items.name: ILLNESS_DAMAGE
items.text: Health lost by someone who catches the island's everyday illness. The chance is the island's disease_risk.

items.name: CROSS_ISLAND_COST
items.text: Extra price paid when buying from another island (only if islands trade).

items.name: BIRTH_CHANCE
items.text: Chance a birth attempt succeeds. Each island gets about two attempts a year, more on a bigger island, and needs room: (4 + 6 x fertility) x its size.

items.name: EVENT_LOG_CAP
items.text: The event log keeps this many of the newest events.

items.name: DISPUTE_SCALE
items.text: Chance a trade is refused = this x average aggression x (1 - average cooperation); STRANGER_DISPUTE times likelier across the sea.

items.name: RAID_SCALE
items.text: Chance a starving adult raids = this x aggression x (1 - cooperation); RAID_SUCCESS is the chance it works.

items.name: RAID_INJURY
items.text: Health a failed raider loses.

items.name: TRUST_DECAY
items.text: Trust keeps this share of its distance from neutral each year.

items.name: PAIR_AGES
items.text: Adults in this age range can form a couple.

items.name: PAIR_CHANCE
items.text: Yearly chance that a single adult with an eligible unrelated neighbour on the island pairs up with the most compatible one (trust, similar cooperation).

items.name: PAIR_TRUST
items.text: Trust a new couple starts with; it grows by PAIR_TRUST_YEARLY each year together.

items.name: MENTOR_MIN_AGE
items.text: A teacher is at least this old.

items.name: MENTEE_AGES
items.text: A pupil is in this age range.

items.name: MENTOR_CHANCE
items.text: Yearly chance a young person gets a lesson from a parent (if experienced) or else the most skilled adult on the island.

items.name: MENTOR_STEP
items.text: A lesson closes this share of the gap in the teacher's best skill. Skills only move toward the teacher's and never past it.

items.name: GRUDGE_RAID
items.text: Grudge a victim holds against a raider (a refused trade gives GRUDGE_QUARREL).

items.name: GRUDGE_DECAY
items.text: Grudges keep this share each year and are forgotten below GRUDGE_MIN.

items.name: FEUD_SCALE
items.text: Retaliation chance = this x (own grudge + FEUD_FRIENDS x friends' grudges) x (0.5 + the victim's aggression), capped at FEUD_MAX.

items.name: FEUD_FRIEND_TRUST
items.text: A friend is someone on the same island whom the victim trusts at least this much (or kin) and who shares the grudge.

items.name: FEUD_TAKE
items.text: Share of the offender's food above need that the victim takes back in a retaliation; the offender also loses FEUD_INJURY health.

items.name: GRUDGE_RETALIATION
items.text: Grudge the offender then holds against the victim, so feuds can escalate.

items.name: MIGRATE_HUNGER
items.text: Hunger motive: an adult who got less than this share of the food they need may leave for a cheaper-food island with room.

items.name: MIGRATE_PRICE_GAIN
items.text: ... where food costs at least this much less. Chance per year: MIGRATE_CHANCE.

items.name: FLIGHT_COOPERATION
items.text: Feud-flight motive: a person at least this cooperative (0-1) ...

items.name: FLIGHT_FEUDS
items.text: ... who is caught up in at least this many live feuds (held or suffered) may leave for the calmest island with room. Chance per year: FLIGHT_CHANCE x feuds / this, at most 0.9.

items.name: TRADE_MOVE_GAIN
items.text: Trade motive: someone may move to an island where a good they have to sell fetches at least this much more.

items.name: TRADE_MOVE_TRADER
items.text: Yearly chance a trader chases a better market; TRADE_MOVE_OTHER for anyone else with a big surplus.

items.name: GENE_TRAITS
items.text: Five traits have two alleles each. A child gets one randomly chosen allele from each parent and its trait is their average (no dominant or recessive alleles).

items.name: GENE_SPREAD
items.text: A founder's two alleles for a trait sit up to this far either side of the value they were given, so founders look the same as without genetics.

items.name: MUTATION_RATE
items.text: Chance that an inherited allele mutates.

items.name: MUTATION_STEP
items.text: A mutation shifts the allele by up to this much; alleles stay between 0 and 1.

items.name: GENE_TRAIT_MIN
items.text: A child's trait is the average of its two alleles, never below this.

items.name: DISASTER_PARAMS
items.value: plague: lethality 0.7, health_hit 50, contact 1.0, goods 0.0, stock 0.0; disease: lethality 0.35, health_hit 30, contact 0.6, goods 0.0, stock 0.0; tsunami: lethality 0.8, health_hit 40, contact 1.0, goods 1.0, stock 0.8; storm: lethality 0.15, health_hit 20, contact 0.5, goods 0.6, stock 0.5; drought: lethality 0.0, health_hit 0, contact 0.0, goods 0.0, stock 0.0
items.text: Per type: lethality (chance an exposed person dies at scale 1), health_hit, contact (share exposed), goods and stock (share destroyed at scale 1).

items.name: DROUGHT_LOSS
items.text: A drought of scale 1 takes this share of farm output and regrowth.

items.name: VULNERABLE_AGES
items.text: Anyone younger or older than this range is VULNERABLE_FACTOR times as likely to die; someone already at 0 health, up to WEAK_FACTOR more.

items.name: DEATH_CAP
items.text: Nobody exposed has more than this chance of dying, whatever the scale.

items.name: RANDOM_DISASTER_SCALE
items.text: A chance disaster (world setting 'chance per year') draws its scale between these.

notes: Lessons change a person's skill but not their alleles, so a taught skill is not passed on to children.
Gene dice have their own random stream. Children no longer follow the old parent-average rule, so a run with genetics is a different world from the same seed without it (world setting 'Genes').
Skills are stored 1 to 10 and cooperation/aggression 0 to 100; an allele is 0 to 1, so a skill is the allele times 10 and a temperament trait the allele times 100.
Scale runs from 0 to 1 for every disaster. 1 is the worst the model has: a plague or tsunami at scale 1 kills most of the people it reaches; 0.5 kills about half as many; 0 does nothing.
The model has no sexes: any two unrelated single adults on one island can become a couple, and (with social life on) children are born only to couples.
Feuds move food and health, never coins. Migration carries all belongings, and the partner and young children go too, so total coins only change when a whole family line dies out.
Total coins = the sum of every living person's wealth. Inequality is the Gini coefficient of those coins: 0 means everyone holds the same, values towards 1 mean a few hold nearly everything.
Dice are seeded from the world seed and the year, so the same world and seed replay the same year. Social life changes births, so a run with it on is a different world from the same seed with it off.

Names: only the first generation can have chosen names. A child is named after the island it was born on (i1 = a, i2 = b ... i7 = g) and a running number for that island, so the 21st person registered on i1 is a21, wherever they later live.

plague.text: One sweep through the islands you choose (all if none). Health damage and deaths among everyone it reaches.

disease.text: An epidemic that lasts several years. Each year about 60% of the people in range are exposed; weaker ones die.

tsunami.text: Hits ONE island (random if none is chosen). Stores, goods and wild stocks are washed away and many drown.

storm.text: Like a tsunami but milder: it destroys part of the goods and stocks and kills few.

drought.text: Lasts several years. Farm output and wild-food regrowth fall; nobody dies directly, they go hungry.

note: These constants are modelling choices, not measurements: change them in sim_constants.py and the outcomes can change.
